source_title: Aston Villa vs Fulham: Key stats and talking points - BBC
source_excerpt:
Aston Villa and Fulham were knocked out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but will both be seeking a third consecutive league win on Saturday night (20:00 GMT).
The hosts have a strong home record in this fixture, with their solitary defeat in 18 Premier League meetings at Villa Park coming in April 2014.
Aston Villa are yet to lose a Premier League game in the month of October under Unai Emery, winning eight times and drawing four. Last Saturday's win over league leaders Manchester City marked the four-year anniversary of Emery's appointment, and on Friday this week he surpassed Martin O'Neill as the club's longest-serving manager since the gilded reign of Ron Saunders from 1974 to 1982.
After admitting he used the difficult first month of the campaign before the international break as an extended pre-season to mould his new-look side, Emery's Villa 2.0 are taking shape. The club's two most expensive signings are more than justifying their hefty price tags, with Johan Manzambi a creative tour de force and Nicolas Jackson scoring six goals in as many games.
Villa reeled off six wins and a draw in seven games across all competitions before Wednesday's limp surrender by mostly fringe players at Bournemouth in a customary early Carabao Cup exit under the Spaniard. "Premier League is the priority," said an unapologetic Emery afterwards.
That being the case, Villa have been meeting their manager's demands of late, earning a league-high 10 points from the past four rounds of matches.
While Villa are in thrall to their Spanish manager, many Fulham supporters are reserving judgement on theirs.
Some of the pressure on Alvaro Arbeloa was alleviated by consecutive 1-0 league wins over promoted opponents, but Wednesday's Carabao Cup defeat at home to struggling Crystal Palace has stirred up the unrest.
That tie was an all-too-familiar tale under Arbeloa of dominating possession but lacking a cutting edge. Fulham average 58% possession in the league this season â the fifth highest â and can be easy on the eye; only Manchester City have strung together more sequences of at least 10 passes, and no side can match Fulham for the volume of those ending in a touch or shot in the opposition penalty area.
There's no lack of effort either, with Arsenal the only side to cover more ground this season. Having improved defensively of late, Fulham's major ongoing issue is that they're not taking their chances.
The Cottagers rank in the league's top 10 for a variety of attacking metrics â including more goal attempts on target than Arsenal â but their shot conversion rate is the fourth worst in the division.
